transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice a week during the spring semester, with soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, supervised by one STEM teacher. Before I can approve this, I need to gather relevant implementation information from each of you. I'd like to hear from the STEM teacher, the school nurse, and the technology coordinator about any considerations I should be aware of. Please go ahead and share what you think I need to know.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important update from my room-safety review, which I completed this week. The review found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be revised before the program can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share findings from my review of the participating students' health records. I found that one student has a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important finding from my review. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program still contains the cloud-storage instruction, so that will need to be updated before the program can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A4
